mechanism_narrative: Accelerating GDP growth, as measured by the year-over-year change in real GDP, signals a strengthening economy that will boost corporate earnings and drive positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: Yield curve inverts (10Y-2Y < 0) during the signal period, indicating a looming recession that will negate the positive earnings impulse.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp drop in industrial production, as measured by the year-over-year change in the INDPRO index, signals a supply shock that will negatively impact S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of months following a -2% YoY drop in INDPRO, indicating the supply shock is not negatively impacting equity prices.

mechanism_narrative: A rapid rise in the unemployment rate, defined as a 0.5 percentage point increase over the past 3 months, signals a weakening labor market that will negatively impact consumer spending and drive negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: Retail sales (RSAFS) grow faster than the prior 6-month average during the signal period, indicating consumer spending is not weakening despite the rising unemployment rate.

mechanism_narrative: A flattening yield curve, defined as the 10-year yield falling below the 2-year yield, signals a looming recession that will drive negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: The yield curve steepens (10Y-2Y > 1%) within 3 months of inverting, indicating the recession signal was false.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp drop in housing starts, defined as a 10% year-over-year decline in the HOUST series, signals a weakening housing market that will negatively impact consumer spending and drive negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: Homebuilder stocks (ITB) outperform the S&P 500 by more than 5% over the 20-day signal period, indicating the housing market weakness is not impacting broader equity markets.

mechanism_narrative: An accelerating pace of job growth, defined as the 3-month moving average of PAYEMS rising faster than the 12-month average, signals a tightening labor market that will boost wage growth and consumer spending, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: Real wage growth (AHE) fails to accelerate in the 3 months following the signal, indicating the labor market tightening is not translating into higher consumer spending power.

mechanism_narrative: A rapid rise in the federal funds rate, defined as a 1 percentage point increase over the past 3 months, signals a tightening monetary policy that will negatively impact S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: High-yield corporate bond spreads (BofA Merrill Lynch US High Yield Option-Adjusted Spread) narrow by more than 50 basis points during the signal period, indicating credit markets are not tightening in response to higher rates.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp drop in real consumer spending, defined as a 5% year-over-year decline in the RSAFS series, signals a weakening consumer sector that will negatively impact S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: Consumer discretionary stocks (XLY) outperform consumer staples (XLP) by more than 2% over the 20-day signal period, indicating consumer spending is not weakening.
